study_guide.title: Cane Becomes a Weather Watcher

pages.text: Cane the Weather Dog woke up and stretched his four paws. "Good morning, world!" he said. "I wonder… what is the weather today?" Cane trotted to the window and looked outside. "All around the Earth is a big blanket of air. Scientists call it the atmosphere," said Cane. "Weather is what the atmosphere is doing right now. Let's find out together!" First, Cane looked up at the sky. "Is it sunny or cloudy?" Then Cane opened the door and felt the air. "Is it hot or cold?" He gave a happy shiver. "A little cool today!" Cane held out a paw. "Is it wet or dry? Is any rain falling?" No rain today — the ground was dry. Then Cane's ears blew back. Whoosh! "Is it windy or calm?"
pages.ask: Can you look outside — what does the sky look like right now? Can you blow like the wind — whooosh?

pages.text: "Sunny, cool, dry, and a little windy," said Cane. "Now I know today's weather! When you look, and feel, and notice — that's called making an observation. That's what real scientists do."
Cane wagged his tail. "A scientist who studies the weather has a special name — a meteorologist. And guess what? A weather watcher like YOU is a meteorologist too!"

"Here's a secret," Cane whispered. "Weather is what's happening today. But when we watch a place for a long, long time, we learn its climate — what the weather is usually like. Weather is what you get today. Climate is what you expect."

Cane grabbed his little notebook. "Every day, I write down what the sky is doing. Sun, clouds, rain, wind — I watch it all. Will you be my weather-watching partner?" "Great job, weather watcher," said Cane. "You looked, you felt, you noticed. You are weather-ready!"

study_guide.rule: Weather is what the atmosphere is doing right now — and a weather watcher looks, feels, and notices.
